note: PROPOSED (CP-CHECK-1, not released). The code that observes what a Check declares in `observes`, carried ON the Check so that the Check's semantic digest covers the exact source. One Check, N collectors: the same fact contract served by a shell script, an Ansible task, a Python SDK call or a raw API request - choosing a language chooses a collector, never another Check. A collector prints ONE observation (kernel $defs/checkObservation: {facts} or {resources}) and decides nothing; it reports EFFECTIVE values (defaults resolved, drop-ins merged - `sshd -T`, not sshd_config), a fact it looked for and did not find is left out (observed absent), and a collector that could not look prints nothing (no observation, inconclusive); the verdict is check-verdict (B.1.10) over that observation, which any tool recomputes without running code. Declaration [] because nothing in this payload changes what passing means - criteria do, and they are kernel. A tool that cannot run a runtime still validates, recomputes and renders. `runtime` is a closed code list plus namespaced URIs for the rest. `privileges` states what the code needs, so a runner can refuse rather than escalate. Credentials and target inventory NEVER appear here: they are runner configuration.
